abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Holography<jats:sup>1</jats:sup> has always held special appeal as it is able to record and display spatial information in three dimensions<jats:sup>2–10</jats:sup>. Here we show how to augment the capabilities of digital holography<jats:sup>11,12</jats:sup> by using a large number of narrow laser lines at precisely defined optical frequencies simultaneously. Using an interferometer based on two frequency combs<jats:sup>13–15</jats:sup> of slightly different repetition frequencies and a lensless camera sensor, we record time-varying spatial interference patterns that generate spectral hypercubes of complex holograms, revealing the amplitudes and phases of scattered wave-fields for each comb line frequency. Advancing beyond multicolour holography and low-coherence holography (including with a frequency comb<jats:sup>16</jats:sup>), the synergy of broad spectral bandwidth and high temporal coherence in dual-comb holography opens up novel optical diagnostics, such as precise dimensional metrology over large distances without interferometric phase ambiguity, or hyperspectral three-dimensional imaging with high spectral resolving power, as we demonstrate with molecule-selective imaging of an absorbing gas.</jats:p>
title: Dual-comb hyperspectral digital holography
